answer: Give each applicant one sealed case holding three specimens keyed to that applicant alone: a walnut plank whose grain is photographed and hashed, a copper rod fingerprinted by its impurity pattern, and an opal chip recorded by its spectrum. The holder assays them in registry order, filing each result before the next seal opens, so assays cannot be batched or shared. A lab spot-checks one result; a copied specimen voids the case. A second identity demands a second case: $410 in sourcing and lab fees plus 22 bench hours, since each fingerprint belongs to one applicant and each seal opens once.
